It is a tool's own project page, not a threat report, so no facts are recorded.

23159a7b614699b40e0cf08cd7ee7a00d67d54b6.summary: VMware Threat Research analysis, published 2021-03-11, of Defray777, a Linux command-line ransomware that encrypts files using hardcoded keys and has been used against VMware ESXi virtualised hosts. The report says it appears to be an evolution of RansomEXX code. Defray777 is typically the final step of a breach that also uses PyXie RAT, Cobalt Strike, LaZagne and Mimikatz. Three Linux samples were analysed, and file metadata was withheld to limit exposure.

239a61a974c62f9f17b838a165c65f5f1ab64fff.summary: Gemini Advisory, a Recorded Future company, reports that FIN7 uses trojanized USB devices built on Arduino-type microcontrollers to inject keystrokes. These run PowerShell that loads the IceBot remote access trojan, giving FIN7 remote access to victim networks. The report lists payload-hosting addresses and command-and-control servers, one with a control panel showing infected systems. It also says FIN7 recently created a fake security company, Bastion Secure, and that its administrators may be involved in building or distributing the USB devices.

238a0dc2d7c417664d146b73a4ade9718a20edbe.summary: Red Canary blog post on hunting for the Rocke actor (also called Iron) in Linux environments. Rocke is associated with cryptocurrency mining payloads and the Xbash malware family, and its campaigns were examined by Talos Group and Unit 42 in 2018 and 2019. The post describes techniques from a recent campaign (public-facing app exploitation, Pastebin-hosted scripts, removal of competing miners, cron persistence, process hiding, timestomping, SSH lateral movement) and suggests endpoint detections, several rated medium confidence.
